decisions.reason: As a low-noise burner closely related to the firm's existing infrared heating know-how, it is something the firm can understand and refine with its current engineering base, so management is more likely to keep it despite its niche character.

This gas infrared plaque heater fits the firm's knowledge base, but with a narrow portfolio and likely overlap with the standard plaque heater, management would be inclined to drop the less clearly differentiated version if early learning has not shown a strong advantage.

A gas infrared luminous radiant heater remains close enough to the firm's core heating competencies that the firm can absorb market feedback and improve it, making retention slightly more likely than withdrawal.

Because this gas-fired infrared tube heater is a product line with several models and sits squarely within the firm's established technical and service capabilities, management would usually keep it as a core extension of the business.

A standard gas infrared plaque heater is a straightforward extension of the firm's existing offer, and its standardized nature makes it easier for the firm to support, learn from, and commercialize successfully.

Since this gas-fired infrared tube heater appears more redundant beside the broader multi-model tube-heater line, management would likely reallocate resources unless it had shown distinctly superior demand or technical learning.
